sentences.text: The animal possessed elongated toes and lower legs that resembled those of modern amphibious or wading birds.
Its upper and lower jaws featured blunt, low-crowned teeth.
A hard, bone-like structure known as the predentary sat at the very tip of the lower jaw.
The pubis bone was slender and measured longer than the femur.
Leg bones were arranged with the tarsometatarsus being the longest, followed by the tibiotarsus, then the femur.
Researchers collected the fossil remains of Khinganornis in May 2017 at the Pigeon Hill locality.
The holotype specimen is housed at Hebei Geo University under the accession number SGM-AVE-2017001.
Its leg proportions and ankle structure suggest a semiaquatic ecology similar to modern wading birds.
Based on its close relatives, Khinganornis likely preferred wading in nearshore aquatic environments.
Phylogenetic analyses classify Khinganornis as a member or close relative of the family Gansuidae.
The genus is classified within the family Gansuidae.
Khinganornis lived during the Aptian age of the Early Cretaceous in Inner Mongolia, China.
The species lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
It is debated how Khinganornis relates to other birds, as different phylogenetic methodologies have produced contrasting evolutionary trees.
